title: Compatibility of comparison with transport along a functor
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be categories [def-nagata-category] and $L:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ a functor. Let $F_C,G_C$ be endofunctors of $\mathcal C$ and $F_D,G_D$ endofunctors of $\mathcal D$. Give natural isomorphisms $\kappa_C:F_C\xrightarrow{\sim}G_C$, $\kappa_D:F_D\xrightarrow{\sim}G_D$ and natural isomorphisms
$$c_F:L\circ F_C\xrightarrow{\sim}F_D\circ L,\qquad c_G:L\circ G_C\xrightarrow{\sim}G_D\circ L.$$
Assume their components satisfy, for every $M\in\mathcal C$,
$$c_{G,M}\circ L(\kappa_{C,M})=\kappa_{D,L(M)}\circ c_{F,M}.$$
For any strict $G_C$-fixed pair $(M,\varphi_M:G_C(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}M)$ [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category], put $u_M=\varphi_M\circ\kappa_{C,M}$ and $\varphi^L_M=L(\varphi_M)\circ c_{G,M}^{-1}$. Then the two resulting structure maps on $L(M)$ agree:
$$\varphi^L_M\circ\kappa_{D,L(M)}=L(u_M)\circ c_{F,M}^{-1}:F_D(L(M))\longrightarrow L(M).$$
This common map is invertible, with inverse $c_{F,M}\circ L(\kappa_{C,M}^{-1}\circ\varphi_M^{-1})$. For any strict $G_C$-fixed pair $(N,\varphi_N)$ and any arrow $h:M\to N$ satisfying $h\varphi_M=\varphi_NG_C(h)$, its image $L(h)$ intertwines these common structure maps. Thus changing from $G$ to $F$ before or after transport by $L$ gives the same objects, the same structure maps, and the same underlying morphisms.

source.place: Entire proof: comparison of the two pullbacks, compatibility with pullback-composition and f, and preservation of the squares

proof.text:
Write compositions in the usual right-to-left order. For each object $M$, compose the assumed comparison square on the left with $c_{G,M}^{-1}$ and on the right with $c_{F,M}^{-1}$. Associativity and the inverse identities give
$$c_{G,M}^{-1}\circ\kappa_{D,L(M)}=L(\kappa_{C,M})\circ c_{F,M}^{-1}.$$
Both sides have source $F_D(L(M))$ and target $L(G_C(M))$. This is cancellation of the two specified isomorphisms, with no faithfulness or exactness assumption on $L$.

source.place: Entire proof: comparison of the two pullbacks, compatibility with pullback-composition and f, and preservation of the squares

proof.text:
Substitute the equality of step 1 into the first proposed structure map. The functor law for composition gives
$$\varphi^L_M\circ\kappa_{D,L(M)}=L(\varphi_M)\circ c_{G,M}^{-1}\circ\kappa_{D,L(M)}=L(\varphi_M)\circ L(\kappa_{C,M})\circ c_{F,M}^{-1}=L(u_M)\circ c_{F,M}^{-1}.$$
Denote this arrow by $a_M:F_D(L(M))\to L(M)$. Thus the two constructions agree as structure maps on the very same object $L(M)$.

source.place: Entire proof: comparison of the two pullbacks, compatibility with pullback-composition and f, and preservation of the squares

proof.text:
Set $w_M=\kappa_{C,M}^{-1}\circ\varphi_M^{-1}:M\to F_C(M)$. The inverse identities show
$$u_M\circ w_M=\varphi_M\circ\kappa_{C,M}\circ\kappa_{C,M}^{-1}\circ\varphi_M^{-1}=\mathrm{id}_M,$$
$$w_M\circ u_M=\kappa_{C,M}^{-1}\circ\varphi_M^{-1}\circ\varphi_M\circ\kappa_{C,M}=\mathrm{id}_{F_C(M)}.$$
Put $v_M=c_{F,M}\circ L(w_M):L(M)\to F_D(L(M))$. Directly,
$$a_M\circ v_M=L(u_M)\circ L(w_M)=L(u_M\circ w_M)=\mathrm{id}_{L(M)},$$
$$v_M\circ a_M=c_{F,M}\circ L(w_M\circ u_M)\circ c_{F,M}^{-1}=\mathrm{id}_{F_D(L(M))}.$$
Here the first equality cancels $c_{F,M}^{-1}\circ c_{F,M}$, and the last equality uses $L(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$. This proves the asserted inverse formula. The same computation applies at $N$.

source.place: Entire proof: comparison of the two pullbacks, compatibility with pullback-composition and f, and preservation of the squares

proof.text:
For an intertwiner $h$ as in the statement, naturality of $\kappa_C$ gives
$$h\circ u_M=h\circ\varphi_M\circ\kappa_{C,M}=\varphi_N\circ G_C(h)\circ\kappa_{C,M}=u_N\circ F_C(h).$$
Naturality of $c_F$ is $F_D(L(h))\circ c_{F,M}=c_{F,N}\circ L(F_C(h))$. Composing with the two inverses yields
$$L(F_C(h))\circ c_{F,M}^{-1}=c_{F,N}^{-1}\circ F_D(L(h)).$$
Applying $L$ to the first displayed equality and using this second one gives
$$L(h)\circ a_M=L(h\circ u_M)\circ c_{F,M}^{-1}=L(u_N)\circ L(F_C(h))\circ c_{F,M}^{-1}=a_N\circ F_D(L(h)).$$
This is precisely the fixed-pair morphism condition, so $L(h)$ intertwines the common invertible structure maps.

source.place: Entire proof: comparison of the two pullbacks, compatibility with pullback-composition and f, and preservation of the squares

proof.text: By the definition of the fixed-pair category, the object and structure map together specify the fixed pair, and its morphisms are the underlying arrows satisfying the displayed condition. Steps 2–3 therefore identify the objects produced by both orders of construction, and step 4 makes their identical underlying arrow $L(h)$ a morphism between them. Both assignments preserve identities and composition since $L(\mathrm{id}_M)=\mathrm{id}_{L(M)}$ and $L(h'\circ h)=L(h')\circ L(h)$. Changing the endofunctor by precomposition also leaves arrows unchanged: its morphism condition is the first calculation of step 4, and its identity and composition laws are inherited from the base category. Thus the two orders give the same objects, structure maps and underlying morphisms, as claimed.

lean.statement: theorem naturalComparisonFunctorTransport {C : Type uC} [Category.{vC} C] {D : Type uD} [Category.{vD} D] (L : C ⥤ D) (FC GC : C ⥤ C) (FD GD : D ⥤ D) (kC : FC ≅ GC) (kD : FD ≅ GD) (cF : FC ⋙ L ≅ L ⋙ FD) (cG : GC ⋙ L ≅ L ⋙ GD) (compat : ∀ M : C, L.map (kC.hom.app M) ≫ cG.hom.app M = cF.hom.app M ≫ kD.hom.app (L.obj M)) (A : Algebra GC) [IsIso A.str] : (kD.hom.app (L.obj A.a) ≫ cG.inv.app A.a ≫ L.map A.str = cF.inv.app A.a ≫ L.map (kC.hom.app A.a ≫ A.str)) ∧ ((cF.inv.app A.a ≫ L.map (kC.hom.app A.a ≫ A.str)) ≫ (L.map (inv A.str ≫ kC.inv.app A.a) ≫ cF.hom.app A.a) = 𝟙 (FD.obj (L.obj A.a))) ∧ ((L.map (inv A.str ≫ kC.inv.app A.a) ≫ cF.hom.app A.a) ≫ (cF.inv.app A.a ≫ L.map (kC.hom.app A.a ≫ A.str)) = 𝟙 (L.obj A.a)) ∧ (∀ (B : Algebra GC) (_hB : IsIso B.str) (h : A ⟶ B), (cF.inv.app A.a ≫ L.map (kC.hom.app A.a ≫ A.str)) ≫ L.map h.f = FD.map (L.map h.f) ≫ cF.inv.app B.a ≫ L.map (kC.hom.app B.a ≫ B.str))
